terms.meaning: The part of a web address after the question mark that carries settings.
A key project event, such as the final investment decision, used to place a project on a timeline.

A small library that handles web addresses and page routing in React.

sections.name: File setup, MilestoneType
sections.title: Imports and milestone choices
sections.what: Brings in the router and memo tools, and defines the four milestone choices a timeline can be based on.
sections.why: Limits milestone choices to four known values.
sections.watch_out: Any other file that matches on this type will need the new value added too.

sections.name: TimeFilter
sections.title: Time filter shape
sections.what: Describes the time filter: a milestone type and optional start and end dates.
sections.watch_out: Dates are stored as text and are not checked as real dates here.

sections.name: QueryFilters
sections.title: Other filter shape
sections.what: Describes the other filters: status, lifecycle stage, maturity, country, technology, minimum and maximum megawatts, search text and segment.
sections.why: Lists every filter a screen can use.
sections.watch_out: The megawatt limits are optional numbers, and nothing checks that the minimum is below the maximum.

sections.name: AllFilters
sections.title: Combined filter shape
sections.what: Joins the time and other filters into one object.
sections.why: Lets callers pass all filters together.

sections.name: parseArray
sections.title: Comma list reader
sections.what: Reads a comma-separated address value into a list, dropping empty pieces. Returns nothing when the value is absent.
sections.why: Lets multi-choice filters, such as several countries, travel in one address value.
sections.watch_out: A single value that itself contains a comma cannot be expressed.

sections.name: parseNumber
sections.title: Number reader
sections.what: Reads an address value as a number, or returns nothing when it is absent.
sections.watch_out: Text that is not a number becomes NaN instead of being rejected.

sections.name: deserializeFilters
sections.title: Address to filter settings
sections.what: Reads the address and builds the time and other filter settings. A missing milestone defaults to any activity. Dates and search text are kept only when present. Address names such as stage map to the lifecycle stage, and segment carries the taxonomy scope.
sections.why: Lets a saved link rebuild the same view.
sections.watch_out: The address names here must match the names the address builder writes, or filters are lost on reload.

sections.name: buildFilterUrl
sections.title: Turning filters into a web address
sections.what: Takes the current filter settings and builds the page address that holds them, such as the address for a list page with a status or country filter already applied. Filters left empty or set to the default are left out of the address.
sections.why: Likely reason: filters live in the web address so a filtered view can be bookmarked, shared, and restored with the browser's back button.
sections.watch_out: Each filter needs a matching name in both this function and the reading side in deserializeFilters, or filters will be saved but never restored.

sections.name: useFilters
sections.title: Hook that reads and changes filters
sections.what: Gives a page its current filters, a way to change them, a way to clear them, and a count of how many filters are active. Changing a filter moves the browser to the new address, which makes the page update.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The pattern suggests the address bar is the single source of truth for filters.
sections.watch_out: Clearing filters or setting a new base path falls back to the current browser path, so calling it from a different page can keep or drop the wrong parts of the address.

summary: Reads the filter choices stored in the web address (such as status, country and size) and turns them into structured filter settings.
purpose: Keeps filter choices in the web address, so a filtered view can be shared or reloaded. The visible parts turn that address text into filter settings.
why: Likely reason: a shared link keeps the same filters. The reasons for the parts not shown are not visible.
how: Defines the four milestone choices (FID, construction start, COD and any activity), the time filter shape, the other filter shape, and the combined shape. parseArray splits comma lists. parseNumber converts text to a number. deserializeFilters reads the address and builds the time and other filter settings, defaulting the milestone to any activity. The useFilters hook and the address builder are not in this packet, so their behavior is not described here.
inputs: The query text from the web address.
outputs: A combined filter object with time and query parts. Missing values stay undefined.
risks: Text that is not a number in a megawatt limit becomes NaN, which can hide or show the wrong projects without an error. Comma lists split on every comma. The address is the source of truth, so bad address text changes the view.
debug: If a filter does not apply, check the exact parameter name in the address. For example, the address uses stage for the lifecycle stage. If a size filter hides everything, check for non-number text. If the time filter is ignored, check the milestone spelling.
